Burgers' Zoo developing world's largest seagrass aquarium

Thursday, 6 August 2026

Royal Burgers’ Zoo is developing the world’s largest seagrass aquarium, with a volume of over 50,000 litres. This vulnerable marine ecosystem depends on light, water movement, water quality, seabed conditions and biological balance.

A crucial ocean ecosystem

Burgers’ Zoo has worked on key marine ecosystems for years. Seagrass meadows provide nursery grounds for young fish, filter water, trap sediment, and store nitrogen and carbon dioxide.

The biggest challenges

Maintaining and growing seagrass is one of the biggest challenges. The team is preparing for future challenges such as managing nutrient levels in the water.

Global research into seagrass restoration

Seagrass meadows are under pressure worldwide. Burgers’ Zoo is monitoring the development scientifically with Wageningen University, NIOZ and the University of Groningen.
